title: Module 3 intro — Control Plane Installation and Configuration

lines: Welcome to Module Three: Control Plane Installation and Configuration.
It's about the software that turns a room of GPU servers into one managed cluster.
Picture a research lab that set up sixty-four GPU nodes by hand, one at a time.
Every node was installed a little differently, and nobody wrote down how.
Within months, driver versions had drifted apart across the cluster.
Jobs that ran on one node crashed on the next, and Fabric Manager refused to start on some.
Then, one Friday evening, the single head node died.
Scheduling, provisioning, and logins went with it, so the whole cluster sat idle all weekend.
Meanwhile, users couldn't run containers on the GPUs at all.
Every researcher built a private software stack, and no result was reproducible.
So the team rebuilt the control plane with NVIDIA Base Command Manager, or BCM.
One software image per node category now provisions every node identically.

lines: They added a second head node, forming an HA pair.
If the active head fails, the passive one takes over, and the cluster keeps running.

Identical nodes, a head node that survives failure, and containers that just work.
